2609.35210.title: Understanding On-Policy Distillation: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective via Sparse Crosscoders
2609.35210.paper_summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) is a widely adopted post-training technique for LLM reasoning. It is commonly believed to transfer knowledge from a stronger teacher, yet what OPD actually distills into the student's internal representations remains unclear. We study this question with sparse crosscoders, which learn one feature dictionary shared by the student before and after OPD and the teacher. Standard crosscoder analyses, however, identify model-specific features but cannot tell how a model's use of its features changes, since all models are encoded into one set of feature activations. We therefore propose the swap readout, which reads each student checkpoint's feature activations on its own, measuring how training changes the student's use of each feature, even for checkpoints unseen by the crosscoder. Across three OPD settings, we find that OPD neither creates features nor passes on the teacher's own, and leaves the firing rates of over 98% of the student's frequently used features within 20%. We further examine the SFT warm-up on the teacher's rollouts that commonly precedes OPD and makes it more effective. Rather than adding features, the warm-up reweights the shared ones in two ways. First, it already raises and lowers many of the features that OPD later raises and lowers, doing part of OPD's work in advance. Second, it changes features that OPD alone would not, notably those for conversation format, reasoning style, and mathematical notation, and these changes persist through OPD. Imposing this reweighting on a directly distilled student's features, without changing its weights, brings its accuracy close to that of the warmed-up student, whereas the same change on shuffled features does not. Together, these findings suggest that OPD reweights existing features rather than acquiring new ones: the student learns from the teacher how to use the features they already share.
2609.35210.paper_summary_zh: 在政策蒸餾（OPD）是廣泛採用的後訓練技術，用於大型語言模型（LLM）的推理。人們普遍認為它可以從更強的教師那裡轉移知識，但OPD實際上在學生的內部表徵中蒸餾了什麼仍然不清楚。我們使用稀疏交叉編碼器來研究這個問題，這些交叉編碼器學習一個特徵字典，該字典在OPD之前和之後以及教師之間共享。然而，標準的交叉編碼器分析識別模型特定的特徵，但無法告訴模型如何使用其特徵的變化，因為所有模型都被編碼為一組特徵激活。因此，我們提出了交換讀出，該方法獨立讀取每個學生檢查點的特徵激活，測量訓練如何改變學生對每個特徵的使用，即使對於交叉編碼器未見過的檢查點。在三個OPD設置中，我們發現OPD既不創建特徵，也不傳遞教師自己的特徵，並且學生經常使用的特徵的激發率超過98%保持在20%以內。我們進一步檢查了教師的回饋中的SFT預熱，這通常在OPD之前進行，並使其更有效。預熱並不是添加特徵，而是以兩種方式重新加權共享特徵。首先，它已經提高和降低了許多OPD稍後會提高和降低的特徵，提前完成了OPD的一部分工作。其次，它改變了OPD單獨不會改變的特徵，特別是對於對話格式、推理風格和數學符號的特徵，這些變化在OPD中持續存在。對直接蒸餾的學生特徵施加這種重新加權，而不改變其權重，使其準確度接近預熱學生的準確度，而對隨機打亂的特徵進行相同的變化則沒有。綜合這些發現表明，OPD重新加權現有特徵，而不是獲取新特徵：學生從教師那裡學習如何使用他們已經共享的特徵。
